links.outcome: false negatives and false positives across workflows
links.effect: Radiologist 2.7% FN/1.2% FP; standalone 1.5%/6.8%; problem-solving 3.2%/0.6%; triage 2.1%/1.7%; safety-net 0.07%/7.6%.
links.quote: All AI-implementation methods changed overall FN and FP with statistical significance (p < 0.001): AI-standalone 1.5 % FN (23/1508; 11 consequences), 6.8 % FP (103/1508); AI-problem-solving 3.2 % FN (48/1508; 31 consequences), 0.6 % FP (9/1508); AI-triage 2.1 % FN (32/1508; 18 consequences), 1.7 % FP (26/1508); AI-safety net 0.07 % FN (1/1508; 1 consequence), 7.6 % FP (115/1508).

links.outcome: standalone versus adjunct fracture diagnosis errors
links.effect: Safety-net had 0.07% FN (1/1508; 1 consequence) versus standalone 1.5% FN (23/1508; 11 consequences), but FP was 7.6% versus 6.8%.
links.quote: Best results were obtained implementing AI as safety net, which eliminates missed fractures with serious clinical consequences; even though false positives are increased, unnecessary treatments are limited.
